Treatment summary
The patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with complaints of neck
pain, stiffness, and headache consistent with whiplash-type cervical injury. The
mechanism of injury is well matched to the reported symptoms, and the clinical picture
reflects the kind and force of the impact. Physical examination documented restricted
cervical range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness, and imaging findings
clearly confirm the soft tissue injury to the neck. No prior injury to the cervical
spine is known from the patient's history or available records.
Care was delivered over ten visits and followed a typical course for this type of
injury, consisting of manual therapy, supervised therapeutic exercise, and a home
stretching program. Symptoms improved steadily, with pain scores and range of motion
gradually returning toawrd baseline, and visit frequency was tapered accordingly as
recovery progressed. Billing records reflect single, appropriate charges for each
service rendered with no repeated or duplicate entries.
At the most recent evaluation the patient reported substantial improvement and
near-resolution of symptoms. Discharge to a self-directed home program is recommended,
with return precautions provided should neck pain or neurological symptoms recur.
